newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent futures close slightly up in dull close.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent futures close slightly up in dull close.

text.p: IPE Brent futures finished Monday's trade marginally stronger, having slipped away from intra-day highs reached on talk of problems with Iraqi oil exports, dealers said.

August Brent last traded at $17.86, up 10 cents on the day in thin trade, but below the day's peak of $17.98. The front-month on New York's West Texas Intermediate contract finished 13 cents higher at $18.96, well below the day's high of $19.18.
Rumours that Iraq will delay resuming crude exports to protest at problems with aid distribution under its oil-for-food deal with the U.N. lifted the market in the mid-afternoon.
But the rumours proved to be old news, buying interest died away, and the market returned to a lethargy brought on by heavy pre-expiry business last Friday.
"There is no volume in there at all now, its just the locals and they helped it come off towards the end," said one dealer.
"We had a pretty active expiry on Friday and that will havee taken the sting out of the market for a day or two," said one player. "I expect it to stay range-bound in the short-term."
Diplomats said Iraq would probably be allowed to sell its full quota of $2 billion worth of oil in the six month term even if a late start compresses all the sales into a shorter period.
